successorSection: Section 497 (Transfers to defraud revenue to be void)
title: Certain Transfers to be Void & Tax Clearance Requirements in Corporate Restructuring (Section 281)

effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Introduced by Income-tax Act, 1961 w.e.f. 1-4-1962. Substituted by Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 1975 w.e.f. 1-10-1975. Standard operating procedure issued via CBDT Circular No. 04/2011. Continues under Income-tax Act, 1961 and transitions to Section 497 of Income-tax Act, 2025.

plainTextSummary: Section 281 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 enacts a statutory anti-alienation protective measure for the Revenue, providing that where an assessee creates a charge on or parts with possession (by way of sale, mortgage, gift, exchange, or any other mode of transfer) of any specified asset during the pendency of any proceeding under the Act or after the completion thereof but before service of notice of demand, such charge or transfer shall be VOID as against any claim in respect of any tax or any other sum payable by the assessee. The covered assets include land, buildings, plant, machinery, shares, securities, and bank fixed deposits exceeding INR 10,000 in value. Under the proviso to Section 281(1), a transfer or charge shall NOT be void if it satisfies either of two independent statutory safe harbors: (i) it is made for adequate consideration and without notice of the pendency of such proceeding or without notice of such tax or other sum payable by the assessee (the Bona Fide Purchaser Exception); or (ii) it is made with the previous written permission of the jurisdictional Assessing Officer (Tax Clearance Certificate under Section 281). CBDT Circular No. 04/2011 lays down the standard operating procedure for seeking prior permission: the assessee must apply at least 30 days prior to the transfer, disclose all pending scrutiny/reassessment proceedings and demands, and furnish adequate alternative security or bank guarantee if demands remain contested. In corporate M&A, business transfers (slump sales), and major capital asset acquisitions, obtaining a Section 281 NOC or verifying bona fide buyer status is an essential closing condition to prevent the Tax Recovery Officer from attaching the acquired assets under the Second Schedule.

keyStatutoryThresholds.provisoSafeHarborOne: Transfer made for adequate consideration without notice of pending proceedings or tax sum payable
keyStatutoryThresholds.provisoSafeHarborTwo: Transfer made with previous written permission of the Assessing Officer
